text.arabic_uthmani: وَقَفَّيْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم بِعِيسَى ٱبْنِ مَرْيَمَ مُصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ ۖ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ ٱلْإِنجِيلَ فِيهِ هُدًۭى وَنُورٌۭ وَمُصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَهُدًۭى وَمَوْعِظَةًۭ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ

words.gloss_range: resumptive coordination that carries the prior Torah-law discourse into the Injil succession stage
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens as continuation and shift together. It carries the preceding Torah-law scene into a new divine-action report, so the Injil stage begins inside the same scriptural sequence rather than as a detached notice.

topics.headline: resumptive stage shift into succession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah continues the prior legal discourse while opening a new prophetic-succession stage.
topics.reason: The opening coordinator links 5:46 to 5:44-45 and launches a divine-action clause rather than an isolated report.

words.gloss_range: completed divine causation of succession, placing a later prophet upon predecessor traces
words.root_gloss_range: following from behind, tracking after traces, and caused succession; locally Form II presents divine orchestration of prophetic sequence
words.prose: {{ar:قَفَّيْنَا}} ({{tr:qaffaynā}}) makes the sequence an act of divine orchestration. The root image of following from behind survives as track-following, and Form II turns that into caused succession: the path of predecessors is named first, then the successor is introduced as the means. Its recurrence with this succession frame (2:87; 57:27) makes the verb a marked scriptural-chain signal.

topics.headline: caused succession along traces
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees succession as divinely caused track-following, not a mere chronological list of prophets.
topics.reason: The Form II perfect with the first-person plural marker presents completed divine agency, while the following path and instrument phrases complete the succession mechanism.

words.gloss_range: upon, marking the predecessor traces as the surface or path of succession
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) turns succession into placement upon a path. The phrase before the prophet's name lets continuity with predecessor traces frame the scene first, while the contrast with the temporal framing in 2:87 shows that this ayah chooses spatial superposition as its image.

topics.headline: trace-path surface before the successor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels succession spatially, as movement upon inherited traces before the successor is named.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the trace noun and attaches to the succession verb, creating a path surface rather than a bare temporal after-phrase.

words.gloss_range: their traces, inherited marks, or predecessor path held by a plural suffix
words.prose: {{ar:ءَاثَٰرِهِم}} ({{tr:āthārihim}}) gives the path substance: not one precedent, but accumulated traces possessed by those before. The same trace language can carry grief or blind inheritance elsewhere (18:6; 43:22-23), but here it is governed by divine succession, so the echo becomes authorized continuity rather than condemned imitation.

topics.headline: plural possessed traces as inherited path
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the succession path as accumulated predecessor traces, not an abstract sequence.
topics.reason: The plural noun with a third-person plural suffix makes the path possessed by prior figures and allows both footprint and transmitted-remnant pressure.

words.gloss_range: by means of the named prophet, with proper-name resonance kept subordinate to the instrumental grammar
words.prose: {{ar:بِعِيسَى}} ({{tr:bi-ʿĪsā}}) is not introduced as an independent subject but as the means of the divine succession act. The proper name can carry contested salvation or purity resonances, and it sits in a recurring prophet, mother-name, and granted-scripture cluster; the role later appears from another discourse stance in 61:6, but local grammar keeps the payoff focused on instrumentality within the succession clause.

topics.headline: named prophet as instrument of succession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the prophet introduced first as the means through whom divine succession is enacted.
topics.reason: The preposition marks instrumentality with the succession verb; debated proper-name resonances remain secondary and do not replace the local grammatical role.

words.gloss_range: son in genitive apposition, construct-bound to the named mother and sealing the identity phrase
words.prose: {{ar:ٱبْنِ}} ({{tr:ibn}}) folds into the preceding name as apposition and requires the following mother-name to complete it. That makes the identity phrase grammatically sealed before the ayah moves to confirmation; any son/building resonance supports continuity but does not turn the word into an independent predicate.

topics.headline: construct sonship binds identity to mother
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that lineage is grammatically fixed before the confirming function is stated.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive in apposition and in construct state, so it depends on the following proper name; building or continuation pressure remains image-level only.

words.gloss_range: the named mother completing the construct identity and anchoring the matronymic formula
words.prose: {{ar:مَرْيَمَ}} ({{tr:Maryam}}) completes the construct identity and makes the matronymic indispensable to the local phrase. The name's origin and resonance remain contested background, while the nearby truth-language echo in 5:75 lets the mother-name and the son's confirming role belong to the same surah identity field.

topics.headline: named mother completes the identity formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prophet identified through the named mother before his confirmatory role begins.
topics.reason: The proper name completes the construct phrase; name-origin or dispute resonances remain cautious background while the local function is identity anchoring.

words.gloss_range: active confirming state of the prophet toward what precedes him from the named scripture
words.root_gloss_range: truthfulness, correspondence, and making true; locally Form II active participle means active validation or confirmation
words.prose: {{ar:مُصَدِّقًۭا}} ({{tr:muṣaddiqan}}) gives the successor a state: he is actively validating what precedes him. The Form II participle moves truth from a quality into verification, and the first occurrence closes the prophet-succession unit before the scripture-grant unit repeats the same confirmation logic. The formula also joins wider confirmation scenes (3:3; 5:48; 61:6).

topics.headline: active confirmation as circumstantial state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees confirmation as the prophet’s active state within succession, not as a static title.
topics.reason: The accusative active participle functions as a circumstantial state attached to the named prophet and prepares the later person-book doubling.

words.gloss_range: for or toward what, fixing the scope of confirmation rather than the instrument of it
words.prose: {{ar:لِّمَا}} ({{tr:li-mā}}) fixes the confirmation's scope. It points the active validation toward what is already before the prophet, and its later repetition makes the two confirmation frames visibly paired.

topics.headline: scope marker for confirmation object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the confirmation is aimed at a defined prior content, not left objectless.
topics.reason: The particle plus relative element introduces the confirmation scope; the instrumental alternative is not the local form.

words.gloss_range: between within the established idiom for prior scripture or content before someone
words.root_gloss_range: separation, between-ness, distinctness, and clarity; locally the idiom selects anterior relation while retaining clarity-from-separation pressure
words.prose: {{ar:بَيْنَ}} ({{tr:bayna}}) begins the familiar before-the-hands idiom. Locally it is not free between-ness alone; it works with the following dual noun to mark prior scripture as set before the confirmer, while the root's separation and clarity pressure remains audible within that idiom.

topics.headline: between-ness inside the prior-scripture idiom
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears prior revelation as something set before the confirmer in an idiom that also keeps distinctness and clarity in view.
topics.reason: The adverb is construct-bound to the following dual noun, so clarity pressure is preserved inside the idiom rather than replacing it.

words.gloss_range: his two hands, completing the idiom for what lies before him and routing the suffix to the prophet in the first frame
words.root_gloss_range: hand, agency, possession, reach, and access; locally the dual form completes the idiom for prior material before the confirmer
words.prose: {{ar:يَدَيْهِ}} ({{tr:yadayhi}}) completes the first before-the-hands formula and routes the suffix to the prophet in this frame. The dual hand image makes prior scripture feel present and reachable before him, while the row set also prepares the later recurrence where the suffix can be heard through the book as well.

topics.headline: dual hands complete the first confirmation idiom
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that precedence is expressed as reachable nearness before the prophet, not only as an abstract earlier date.
topics.reason: The genitive dual noun completes the idiom governed by the preceding adverb; hand-root power and access senses stay subordinate to the idiom.

words.gloss_range: from or of, explicating the prior content as the named scripture while allowing a limited partitive question
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) narrows what stands before the prophet by specifying the named scripture that follows. The partitive question remains grammatically visible, but the local payoff is explication: both confirmation frames return to the same prior-scripture anchor.

topics.headline: explicative link to the prior scripture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the named scripture as the specified content of what stands before the confirmer.
topics.reason: The preposition specifies the following named scripture; partitive force is possible as a question, but local function is explicative anchoring.

words.gloss_range: the named prior scripture, locally the fixed object of confirmation with cautious instruction and hidden-fire resonance
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ}} ({{tr:at-tawrāti}}) names the prior scripture that the confirmation faces. Its instruction and hidden-fire resonances are kept cautious, while the local structure makes it the anchor that will return again in the second confirmation clause. The guidance-and-light description from 5:44 also prepares the echo that the Injil description takes up.

topics.headline: named prior scripture as confirmation anchor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prior scripture as the fixed anchor for the prophet’s confirmation and for the later book-confirmation clause.
topics.reason: The proper noun is governed by the specifying preposition; derivational fire or instruction resonances remain secondary to its local role as named scripture.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector joining the succession clause to the scripture-grant clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pivots from the prophet placed in succession to the scripture granted to him. The connector keeps the two divine acts joined but distinct: first the person enters the chain, then the book is bestowed.

topics.headline: pivot from person succession to scripture grant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah joins two divine acts: causing succession and granting scripture.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates two divine-action clauses while preserving their distinct roles in the ayah movement.

words.gloss_range: We gave him, a completed divine grant with giver and recipient compressed into the verb
words.root_gloss_range: coming, arrival, bringing, and giving; locally Form IV makes scripture arrive to the recipient as a divine grant
words.prose: {{ar:ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ}} ({{tr:ātaynāhu}}) compresses giver, act, and recipient into one completed grant. The arrival-root pressure makes the giving feel like caused arrival of scripture, and the sequence differs from 2:87 by narrating succession first and bestowal next. Within the surah, the gift frame also answers covenantal giving language (5:12).

topics.headline: completed divine grant of scripture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the book as bestowed through divine agency, not simply possessed by the prophet.
topics.reason: The perfect Form IV verb with speaker and object affixes marks completed divine giving to the named recipient.

words.gloss_range: the named Gospel scripture as direct object of the divine grant, with loanword and good-news resonance kept subordinate
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْإِنجِيلَ}} ({{tr:al-Injīla}}) is first the direct object of the divine grant. Good-news, bringing-forth, and loanword-pronunciation pressures remain secondary, while the ayah makes the book enter as bestowed scripture before it is described as containing guidance and light, confirming the prior scripture, and grounding the next judgment command (5:47).

topics.headline: gifted scripture before its functions unfold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the scripture first as a bestowed object before the ayah describes what it contains and does.
topics.reason: The proper scripture name is the direct object of the giving verb; pronunciation, loanword, and origin resonances do not override that object role.

words.gloss_range: in it, opening a nominal content clause that locates guidance and light inside the scripture
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهِ}} ({{tr:fīhi}}) opens a content clause inside the granted scripture. The phrase interrupts the movement from gift to confirmation so the reader first learns what is in the book: guidance and light, not merely an external authority label.

topics.headline: container phrase for scripture contents
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees guidance and light as contents located within the scripture before its outward function is named.
topics.reason: The preposition plus pronoun opens a nominal clause whose pronoun refers to the granted scripture.

words.gloss_range: guidance as internal content of the scripture, indefinite and directional rather than mere information
words.root_gloss_range: guiding, leading, directing, and showing the way; locally guidance is contained in the scripture before being redeployed as outward function
words.prose: {{ar:هُدًۭى}} ({{tr:hudan}}) first names guidance as content within the scripture. The word keeps a led-movement image: guidance is conducted toward a destination rather than static information, and its indefinite form lets the quality feel expansive. Its later recurrence will shift from internal content to outward function, while the shared guidance-and-light sequence echoes the prior scripture description (5:44).

topics.headline: guidance inside the scripture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices guidance first as something contained in the scripture before the final phrase turns guidance outward toward its audience.
topics.reason: The nominative indefinite noun is part of the nominal content clause and later reappears in a different syntactic slot.

words.gloss_range: additive coordination pairing guidance with light inside the content clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps guidance and light paired inside the same content clause. It does not start a new clause or subordinate light as a gloss; it adds a second coequal quality within the scripture.

topics.headline: coordination creates a guidance-light pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices guidance and light as coequal contents rather than one term explaining the other.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates two nominative contents inside the same nominal clause.

words.gloss_range: light as visible, evidence-producing content joined to guidance inside the scripture
words.root_gloss_range: light, illumination, visibility, and fire-adjacent brightness; locally it is revelatory visibility, not punitive fire or decoration
words.prose: {{ar:نُورٌۭ}} ({{tr:nūrun}}) adds visibility to direction. As a nominative partner to guidance, it makes the scripture evidentiary and illuminating; fire-pressure remains lexical background, not local punishment. The pairing belongs to the wider book-light field, including 5:15.

topics.headline: light as evidentiary visibility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the scripture not only directing but making things visible and evidential.
topics.reason: The nominative noun is coordinated as content; fire-pressure rows are lexical background and do not make punishment the local sense.

words.gloss_range: connector beginning the second confirmation clause after the internal content clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the hinge after the content clause. The ayah has named what is in the scripture; this connector turns back to what the scripture does, beginning the second confirmation frame.

topics.headline: hinge from contents to function
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah move from what the scripture contains to what it does in relation to prior revelation.
topics.reason: The connector starts the second confirmation clause and preserves the internal-content clause as a distinct step.

words.gloss_range: active confirmer applied to the scripture, with role pressure between circumstance, coordination, and purpose
words.root_gloss_range: truthfulness, correspondence, and active validation; locally the same Form II participle transfers confirmation from prophet to book
words.prose: {{ar:مُصَدِّقًۭا}} ({{tr:muṣaddiqan}}) repeats the confirmation role with the book now in view. Its exact syntax carries pressure between circumstantial, coordinated, and purpose readings, but the local payoff is stable: messenger and message jointly validate the same prior scripture. The same confirmation formula also appears in the prophet's own voice (61:6).

topics.headline: book becomes the second active confirmer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees messenger and message jointly confirming the same prior scripture.
topics.reason: The accusative participle admits role pressure, but the repeated frame and local coordination transfer active confirmation from the person to the scripture.

words.gloss_range: repeated scope marker introducing the object of the book’s confirmation
words.prose: {{ar:لِّمَا}} ({{tr:li-mā}}) repeats the earlier scope frame. The confirming subject has shifted from the prophet to the scripture, but the object-marker stays the same, making the second frame deliberate rather than decorative repetition.

topics.headline: repeated scope frame for the book
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second confirmation deliberately reuse the first frame under a new confirming head.
topics.reason: The same particle construction repeats after the second confirming participle and marks the scope of confirmation.

words.gloss_range: the second between element rebuilding the same prior-scripture idiom for the book’s confirmation
words.root_gloss_range: separation, between-ness, distinctness, and clarity; locally reused inside the same before-the-hands idiom
words.prose: {{ar:بَيْنَ}} ({{tr:bayna}}) rebuilds the same before-the-hands idiom in the second confirmation. The repetition is architectural: it locks the book's confirmation to the prophet's confirmation while preserving the root pressure of distinctness and clarity inside the idiom.

topics.headline: repeated idiom locks the two frames together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the architecture: the book-confirmation clause reconstructs the same prior-scripture idiom.
topics.reason: The second occurrence rebuilds the same construct idiom; root clarity pressure remains embedded in the idiomatic frame.

words.gloss_range: the second dual-hands idiom, with the suffix able to be heard through the prophet or the scripture in the repeated frame
words.root_gloss_range: hand, agency, possession, reach, and access; locally the dual form completes the repeated idiom and creates controlled antecedent pressure
words.prose: {{ar:يَدَيْهِ}} ({{tr:yadayhi}}) repeats the dual-hands formula under the book-confirmation frame. The suffix can still resonate with the prophet, while the new head lets the scripture frame press forward; this controlled ambiguity helps the repeated confirmation pattern bind person and book.

topics.headline: second hands phrase carries controlled ambiguity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repeated idiom can keep the prophet in view while also letting the book-confirmation frame press forward.
topics.reason: The suffix is grammatically singular masculine and occurs under a new confirming head, so the antecedent pressure is real but controlled by the repeated formula.

words.gloss_range: second specifying preposition that reanchors the repeated confirmation frame to the same named scripture
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) closes the repeated confirmation frame by reintroducing the same specifying link. Because the confirming head has changed, the repetition matters: the book is anchored to the same prior scripture as the prophet.

topics.headline: second specifying link closes the repeated frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the second confirmation returns to the same prior-scripture anchor.
topics.reason: The preposition repeats the earlier specifying function after the second before-the-hands idiom.

words.gloss_range: the same named prior scripture repeated as the fixed axis of both confirmation clauses
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ}} ({{tr:at-tawrāti}}) returns as the same named prior scripture, not a new source. Its repetition makes the prior scripture the fixed axis: the prophet confirms it, and the granted scripture confirms it as well.

topics.headline: same prior scripture fixed across both clauses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prior scripture become the stable axis around which both the prophet and the scripture are positioned.
topics.reason: The second mention is governed by the same specifying construction and prevents the two confirmation clauses from drifting apart.

words.gloss_range: additive connector that moves from confirmation into the final guidance function chain
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) turns from confirmation into function. It adds guidance to the final chain without making it merely an explanation of confirmation, so the ayah moves from relation between scriptures to benefit for an audience.

topics.headline: pivot into beneficiary-directed functions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah move from inter-scripture confirmation to what the scripture provides for its audience.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates guidance into the final chain after confirmation and begins the move toward the beneficiary phrase.

words.gloss_range: guidance as outward function or purpose for the scripture’s audience, echoing but changing the earlier internal content slot
words.root_gloss_range: guiding, leading, directing, and showing the way; locally the repeated noun moves from contained quality to applied orientation
words.prose: {{ar:هُدًۭى}} ({{tr:hudan}}) repeats the guidance word but changes its job. The first occurrence was content in the scripture; this one stands in the final function chain, directing the scripture outward toward the guarded audience. The recurrence links with guidance-audience formulas (2:2; 3:138) without making the two local slots identical.

topics.headline: guidance shifts from content to function
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that repeated guidance is semantic movement: first inside the scripture, then directed outward toward recipients.
topics.reason: The second occurrence stands in an accusative function chain rather than the earlier nominative content clause.

words.gloss_range: coordination pairing final guidance with admonition as two beneficiary-directed functions
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pairs the final guidance with admonition. The connector makes admonition coequal rather than a modifier, and it adds a purpose-specific element that was not named in the earlier guidance-and-light content clause.

topics.headline: final pair of direction and admonition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees admonition added as a coequal final function, not a subordinate gloss of guidance.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates the final admonition noun with guidance in the same function chain.

words.gloss_range: admonition as protective corrective counsel in the final function chain, with variant case contrast noted
words.root_gloss_range: admonishing, warning, counsel, and restraint before harm; locally protective correction coordinated with guidance
words.prose: {{ar:مَوْعِظَةًۭ}} ({{tr:mawʿiẓatan}}) adds protective counsel to the final function chain. The word is corrective warning before harm, not punitive threat, and its gerund form gives the counsel event-like weight. The nominative variant would let admonition stand more independently, but the local accusative keeps it coordinated with guidance; the phrase also matches the guidance-admonition audience formula (3:138), where guidance directs, admonition warns protectively, and the guarded audience receives both, and it adds an element beyond the prior guidance-and-light description (5:44).

topics.headline: protective admonition in the final function chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final function as corrective counsel joined to guidance, not as harsh punishment or bare information.
topics.reason: The canonical accusative keeps the noun coordinated in the final function chain; the nominative variant is useful as contrast because it would make the admonition more independent.

words.gloss_range: for the guarded, self-shielding audience, with the lām specifying the recipients of final guidance and admonition
words.root_gloss_range: guarding, shielding, protecting, and taking protective restraint; locally Form VIII active participle names an audience class of self-guarding recipients
words.prose: {{ar:لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ}} ({{tr:li-l-muttaqīna}}) lands the ayah on recipients. The prefixed beneficiary marker can be heard as prioritizing or restricting the audience, and it may attach narrowly to admonition or broadly to the guidance-admonition pair; either way, the final word names a definite class of self-guarding people. The closure joins wider guidance-audience formulas (2:2; 3:138), resonates with truth-and-guarding language (2:177), and prepares the next judgment command (5:47).

topics.headline: guarded audience as closure landing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah closes not only on scripture continuity but on the audience positioned to receive guidance and admonition.
topics.reason: The benefactive preposition specifies the recipients of the final function chain; scope can be heard narrowly or chain-wide, but the closure clearly names the guarded audience.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction wa-qaffayna ala atharihim, followed by two instances of musaddiqan.
baseline_models.mechanism: A successor is set onto predecessors' surviving track, and repeated confirmation makes the succession a verifying relay rather than an erasure of the Torah.

activation_trace.role: Following one thing with another supplies the ordered succession track.
Travel on a predecessor's trace makes the track explicitly inherited.
Realizing a prior word or promise makes both confirmations active rather than verbal only.

changed_reading.before: Jesus simply comes later and assents to an older Torah.
changed_reading.after: Jesus is deliberately placed on a predecessor track, and the Gospel carries that track forward by actively verifying it.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The formula musaddiqan lima bayna yadayhi min al-tawrah occurs twice.
baseline_models.mechanism: The doubled spatial idiom locates the Torah in an accessible foreground, while confirmation describes an enacted relation to what is presently faced.

activation_trace.role: The interval or middle between parties supplies a relational space rather than bare chronology.
What is between the hands is before, near, and available to the confirmer.
Fulfillment turns proximity into practical verification.

changed_reading.before: The Torah is only a chronologically prior document.
changed_reading.after: The Torah is a near-at-hand interlocutor twice faced and practically verified by Jesus and the Gospel.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Fihi hudan wa-nur, followed by wa-hudan wa-maw'izatan lil-muttaqin.
baseline_models.mechanism: Repeated guidance brackets illumination and heart-softening warning, forming a navigation system that both shows a route and trains the traveler to avoid harm.

activation_trace.role: Gentle indication toward a road or truth supplies directional guidance twice.
Illumination makes the guided route perceptible.
A warning that softens the heart converts visibility into affective restraint.
Placing oneself in protection identifies the posture in which that restraint operates.

changed_reading.before: The Gospel offers informative teaching to an already pious audience.
changed_reading.after: The Gospel is protective navigation: it shows, illuminates, warns, and thereby sustains a self-guarding mode of travel.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening offering scene ties divine acceptance specifically to the muttaqin; the focus ending therefore describes not merely an audience label but a receptive posture in which admonition can be taken in.

activation_trace.role: Heart-softening warning is the material whose reception is at issue.
Self-placement in protection names the focus audience's active posture.
Acceptance with satisfaction makes receptivity, not mere exposure, the operative relation.
The same self-protective designation is made the condition associated with acceptance.

structural_cues: The first context ayah closes its accepted and rejected offering contrast with min al-muttaqin, while 5:46 closes with lil-muttaqin.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies acceptance and the shared muttaqin designation; I infer that the acceptance relation analogically sharpens how counsel is received. A live alternative is that muttaqin only names moral character and says nothing about reception.

changed_reading.before: For the pious identifies a fixed recipient class.
changed_reading.after: The admonition enters a reception loop: self-protection makes counsel receivable, and received counsel renews self-protection.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier occurrences of nar activate the fire branch of the same packet root used by focus nur; illumination and warning now function together as route visibility under a hazard from which the context says there is no exit.

activation_trace.role: Light supplies visibility for the protective route.
Warning converts visible danger into restraint before exposure.
The kindled fire branch supplies the first concrete hazard opposed to protective illumination.
The repeated fire is an enclosing destination that cannot be escaped after entry.

structural_cues: Nar appears in the punishment sequence before the focus, and 5:37 explicitly denies exit; the focus later couples nur with maw'iza and taqwa.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the light/fire branch contrast and the protective ending; I assign the directional arrow from illumination and warning toward avoiding fire. The live alternative is that focus nur remains purely epistemic.

changed_reading.after: Light is preventive route visibility under terminal hazard, with admonition turning what is seen into protective action.

context_deltas.mechanism: Words are tilted away after their placements, while Torah custodians are charged to guard and witness; following traces and confirming thus become a discipline of detecting displacement and maintaining a faithful relation to surviving material.

activation_trace.role: Trace-following supplies the method for testing continuity through succession.
A surviving mark supplies inspectable evidence of what preceded.
Truthful correspondence is the criterion applied to the inherited marks.
Tilting away from a direction supplies the mechanism of textual distortion.
A thing's assigned placement makes distortion legible as displacement from a settled location.
Guarding and attending to the Torah supplies the custodial obligation.
Testimony grounded in knowledge makes custody publicly accountable.

structural_cues: The distortion, custody, and witness language immediately precedes the Torah-Gospel succession.
The focus repeats confirmation on both sides of the Gospel's internal qualities.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies displacement, guarding, witnessing, and surviving traces; I infer that confirmation tests and may repair relational placement, not that it reconstructs a wholly lost text. A live alternative is simple attestation without a repair function.

changed_reading.before: Confirmation is a general statement that the Torah is true.
changed_reading.after: Confirmation is trace-sensitive custody: it detects tilted placement, preserves inherited evidence, and witnesses continuity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The exact guidance-and-light pair first characterizes the Torah and then the Gospel, while judgment is commanded through each corpus; the pair is therefore a successive operative charter, not decorative praise.

activation_trace.role: Directional indication supplies the Gospel's first repeated function.
Illumination makes that direction publicly usable.
The same directional function is explicitly located in the Torah.
The same illumination function completes the exact Torah-side pair.
Judgment between people makes Torah guidance operative in decisions.
The corresponding command makes Gospel guidance operative for its people.

structural_cues: The phrase fihi hudan wa-nur is reproduced across 5:44 and 5:46.
Judgment by revealed material frames the focus on both sides.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exact phrase identity and parallel judgment language; I infer a shared functional charter rather than identical contents. A live alternative is that guidance and light are honorific descriptions with no specific judicial force.

changed_reading.before: The Gospel independently contains general spiritual guidance and light.
changed_reading.after: The Gospel receives the Torah's operative guidance-light charter in a new relay and is meant to mediate concrete judgment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The confirmation formula recurs for the next Book beside oversight, a distinct source and clear path for each community, and competition toward goods; confirmation secures lineage while preserving differentiated routes and tests.

activation_trace.role: Active fulfillment anchors continuity with the Torah.
The prior revelation remains present before the confirming bearer.
The same fulfillment relation is repeated for the succeeding Book.
The same near-at-hand relation confirms a recurrent architecture of revelation.
Witnessing and care add evaluative oversight to confirmation.
A visible water source supplies a distinct accessible channel for each community.
A clear path makes differentiation directional rather than arbitrary.
Racing forward turns differentiated paths into an active test.
Movement toward beneficial good supplies the test's practical criterion.

structural_cues: 5:48 repeats the focus confirmation-and-before-hands formula, then says each has a shir'a and minhaj and commands a race toward goods.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies confirmation, oversight, plurality of channels, and a race; I infer continuity-with-difference rather than content identity. A live alternative is that the differentiated assignments are communal only and do not qualify the relation between texts.

changed_reading.before: Confirming the Torah means that the Gospel simply repeats it.
changed_reading.after: Confirmation stabilizes revelatory lineage without flattening it: each relay can retain its own channel, path, oversight, and practical test.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the focus, qisas tracks injury by equivalence but tasaddaqa relinquishes that matched claim; trace-following and repeated musaddiqan can therefore carry a law forward by realizing a forgiving surplus rather than mechanically reproducing it.

activation_trace.role: Equivalent requital supplies a legal form of following an injury's track.
Relinquishing a due claim supplies the voluntary release that interrupts exact matching.
Following after predecessors transfers the track mechanism into revelatory succession.
Travel on a prior trace anchors the new movement in what came before.
Fulfillment allows confirmation to realize the prior law rather than copy its surface.

structural_cues: 5:45 moves from exact body-for-body equivalence to voluntary remission, and 5:46 immediately follows with trace language and two forms of s-d-q.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies legal matching, relinquishment, succession, and two s-d-q branches; I infer that the Gospel may fulfill Torah by carrying its law toward remission. A live alternative is that tasaddaqa concerns only an injured claimant and does not inflect musaddiqan.

changed_reading.before: Confirmation means reproducing the prior rule faithfully.
changed_reading.after: Confirmation may make the prior rule true by carrying its trace into voluntary remission, so continuity can generate forgiving surplus.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-activates an idiom with literal and juridical hands, so it is surprising; it remains anchored in the focus's doubled yadayhi and the packet's hand branches. Render it as a secondary agency resonance, not as a replacement for the ordinary before-his-hands idiom.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The two occurrences of bayna yadayhi.

activation_trace.role: What stands before the hands supplies an available scriptural foreground.
Hands extended or withheld from killing make the hand a site of ethical agency.
Attributing deeds to hands makes bodily agency answerable for what it produces.
Acquired outcome links the hand's action to consequence.

changed_reading.before: Before his hands only marks chronological priority.
changed_reading.after: The inherited Torah also occupies the accountable foreground of action: confirmation concerns what a bearer does with revelation placed before him.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The move uses the form-distant th-w-r target bundled with focus athar, so it is deliberately strange; it remains valid as a packet-supplied split-root material analogy joined to explicit displacement in 5:41. Render it as exploratory reactivation imagery, not as a claim that athar lexically means textual restoration.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Ala atharihim inside the succession construction.

activation_trace.role: Stirring a thing from its place supplies an activation image for latent traces.
Following the track keeps the strange activation tied to succession.
Directional tilting supplies the contextual disturbance that requires renewed inspection.
Assigned locations make moved material detectable as displaced.

changed_reading.before: Succession follows stable footprints already lying in place.
changed_reading.after: Succession may reactivate displaced scriptural traces, bringing latent material back into inspectable motion while still following the inherited track.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: Reading the gift through the watercourse branch is a cross-domain material analogy; it remains anchored in ataynahu, fihi, and the contents named inside the Gospel. Render it as conduit imagery for transmission, not as a lexical translation of atayna.

activation_trace.role: A watercourse that directs flow supplies the Gospel's conduit image.
Guidance is what the conduit carries toward a route.
Light is the perceptible effect distributed through that channel.

changed_reading.before: The Gospel is a bounded object handed to Jesus.
changed_reading.after: The given Gospel can be pictured as an opened conduit through which guidance and light enter an already traced revelatory landscape.

strongest_changes: Confirmation became trace-sensitive custody under distortion, guarding, and witness.
The exact Torah-Gospel guidance-and-light mirror made the Gospel an operative judicial relay rather than a replacement.
The differentiated channels of 5:48 showed that confirmation preserves continuity without flattening distinct paths.
The immediate qisas and tasaddaqa sequence opened an exploratory reading of confirmation as fulfillment through remission rather than replication.
summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly reused focus roots in materially different settings: muttaqin governed acceptance, nur faced nar, hands carried agency and liability, and s-d-q moved from confirmation to relinquishing a claim. Those recurrences changed the focus more than broad thematic similarity did.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the remission branch of s-d-q in 5:45 should materially inflect musaddiqan or is only a provocative adjacency.
Whether the nur and nar contrast is semantically active here or chiefly an artifact of the packet's shared root resolution.
How far 5:48's differentiated paths qualify the Torah-Gospel relation rather than only later communal assignments.
Whether the split th-w-r activation can support prose beyond a tightly marked material analogy.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Revelation advances by following retained traces.** Fixed **ق ف و / B001** (“following a trace and succession”) supplies the forward chain, while fixed **ء ث ر / B003** (“remaining sign that points to what was”) supplies what remains available to follow. The ayah repeats confirmation of what is before Jesus; 5:48 likewise describes the new book as confirming prior scripture before assigning each community an access-way and clear path. The Gospel reads as a guided continuation that verifies and extends a path.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, önden giden bir kişinin ardından gitmeyi ve onun bıraktığı yoldan varlığını belirleyerek ilerlemeyi birlikte destekler.

lexicalization_scope.note: Takip bildiren söz öbeği ile öncekinin yolunu gösteren ad kullanımı ayrı tutulur ve yalın bir iz anlamında birleştirilmez.

concept_map.definition: Önden giden birinin ardından, onun geçtiğini gösteren belirtileri kılavuz edinerek ilerlemek veya önce gidenin geçtiğini gösteren yoldur.

error_profile.preserves: Önce giden kişiye göre ardıllık ilişkisini korur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel ettirgen hareket çekirdeği korunur; toprağı eşeleme, canlıyı kaldırma ve saklı bilgiyi araştırma yalnız kendi kalıplarına bağlı uzmanlaşmalar olarak tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir etkenin bir şeyi bulunduğu durgun ya da gizli durumdan çıkararak kaldırması, hareketlendirmesi veya açığa çıkarmasıdır. Kur'an ilmini yoğun araştırmayla ortaya koymak bu işlemin bağlı düşünsel uzantısıdır.

facets.statement: Bir etken, başka bir şeyi bulunduğu yerden veya durumdan çıkarıp hareketlendirir.
Toprağı eşelemek, tozu kaldırmak ve oturan ya da saklanan bir canlıyı yerinden kaldırmak somut uzmanlaşmalardır.
Kur'an ilmini derinlemesine araştırarak ortaya çıkarmak, fiziksel kaldırmanın yalnız bu bağlı kullanımda görülen düşünsel uzantısıdır.

يدخل فيه البنية اسما للكعبة أو بيت الله، وما ذكرته المصادر من تسمية مكة البنية.

branches.branch_image_ar: المَبْناة بيت أو غطاء من أدم
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه المبناة كهيئة القبة أو الستر من أدم، والنطع أو الحصير أو العيبة، والبناء المبسوط في المطر أو على المتاع.
يدخل فيه القوس البانية أو باناة عند طيئ، وهي التي لزقت بوترها حتى يكاد ينقطع.

branches.branch_image_ar: بناء الرجل على أهله ودخوله بها
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه بنى على أهله بمعنى زفها أو دخل بها، والباني بمعنى العروس، مع تعليل القبة التي تضرب عند الدخول.

branches.branch_image_ar: البُنُوَّة والنسب وما ينسب إلى منشأ
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الابن والبنت والبنون والأبناء والبنات والبنوة، والتبني، وما يسمى ابنا أو بنتا لأنه يحصل من جهة شيء أو تربيته أو خدمته أو ملازمته.

branches.branch_image_ar: تسميات الابن والبنت للأشياء المتفرعة أو الصغيرة
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه بنيات الطريق للطرق الصغار، والبنات للتماثيل الصغار، وبنات المساجد للحصى، وبنت الأرض للحصاة، وابن الأرض للبقل.

branches.branch_image_ar: البَواني أضلاع ودعائم يستقر بها الشيء
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه البواني لأضلاع الزور، والبوان أو البوائن لأعمدة البيت، وألقى بوانيه بمعنى أقام واطمأن.
يدخل فيه بنى لحم فلان طعامه إذا عظمه من الأكل أو سمنه.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı yalanın karşıtı olan söz doğruluğu olarak kurar ve daha özel olarak sözün hem konuşanın iç inancına hem de anlattığı gerçeğe uymasını ister. Bu nedenle dal, genel doğruluk kavramına genişletilmeden söz ve bildirim alanında tutulmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın biçimdeki söz doğruluğunu temel alır; konuşmada doğruyu söyleme ve bir sözün doğruluğunu kabul etme gibi yapıya bağlı kullanımları ayrıca sınırlar.

concept_map.definition: Bir sözün yalan olmaması ve hem söyleyenin iç inancıyla hem de hakkında konuşulan gerçekle uyuşmasıdır.

facets.statement: Söylenen söz yalanın karşıtıdır ve gerçeği bildirir.
Tam uygunluk, sözün hem konuşanın iç inancıyla hem de bildirilen durumla uyuşmasını gerektirir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, söz doğruluğunu yalanın karşıtı sayar; ayrıntılı açıklama, söz ile iç inanç ve dış gerçeklik arasında birlikte uygunluk arar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Söz doğruluğunun hem içtenlik hem de gerçekliğe uygunluk koşulunu birlikte anlatan genel karşılıktır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Konuşanın inancı ile anlattığı durum arasındaki iki yönlü uygunluğun açıklanması gereken bağlamlarda kullanılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yalnızca vaat veya savaşta gereğini yapmayı değil, bir tahmini gerçekleştirmeyi, bir sözü onaylamayı ve önceki bir bildiriyi destekleyip doğrulamayı da kapsar. Bu nedenle dal, salt vaat yerine getirme olarak değil; söz, beklenti veya iddiayı gerçekleşme, eylem ya da onayla doğrulama alanı olarak yeniden çerçevelenmelidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım ortak doğrulama ve gerçekleştirme çekirdeğini verir; savaş, tahmin, önceki bildiri ve konuşmayı onaylama anlamlarını yalnızca kendi yapılarında geçerli uzmanlaşmalar olarak ayırır.

concept_map.definition: Bir söz, beklenti, vaat veya iddiayı gerçekleşme, eylem ya da onay yoluyla doğru çıkarmak ve gerektiğinde söyleneni fiilen yerine getirmektir. Savaşta gereğini yapma, tahminin gerçekleşmesi ve önceki bir bildiriyi destekleme bu çekirdeğin yapıya bağlı görünümleridir.

facets.statement: Bir söz, beklenti veya iddia gerçekleşme, eylem ya da onayla doğru çıkarılır.
Savaş bağlamında kişi gereğini yerine getirir, sebat eder ve eylemiyle sözünün hakkını verir.
Bir tahminin veya beklentinin doğru çıkması da gerçekleşme yoluyla doğrulamadır.
Bir sözün doğruluğunu kabul etmek veya önceki bir bildiriyi desteklemek onay yoluyla doğrulamadır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak çekirdek, bir söz veya beklentinin eylemle, gerçekleşmeyle ya da onayla doğrulanmasıdır; savaşta gereğini yapma, tahminin çıkması ve önceki bildiriyi destekleme bu çekirdeğin farklı gerçekleşmeleridir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi iyilik amacıyla maldan çıkarılan yardımı, kişinin bir hakkından vazgeçmesini, yardımı vereni ve hayvanlara ilişkin payları toplayan görevliyi kapsar. Geçici çerçevenin her türlü zorunlu hakkı niyet koşuluyla bu dala katması kanıtta açık değildir; tanım, mali yardım ve haktan bağışlayarak vazgeçme çekirdeğiyle sınırlandırılmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın mali yardım anlamı temel alınır; bir haktan vazgeçme yapısı ile veren ve toplayan kişi adları ayrı, yapıya bağlı yüzler olarak korunur.

concept_map.definition: Bir kimsenin iyilik ve manevi yakınlaşma amacıyla malından çıkarıp verdiği yardım veya kendi hakkından bağışlayarak vazgeçmesidir. Alan ayrıca yardımı veren kişiyi ve hayvanlara ilişkin yardım paylarını toplayan görevliyi belirten türev kullanımları kapsar.

facets.statement: Kişi kendi malından iyilik ve manevi yakınlaşma amacıyla bir pay çıkarıp verir.
Kişinin kendi hakkından bağışlayarak vazgeçmesi de mali yardım gibi değerlendirilir.
Yardımı veren kimse, verme eylemindeki katılımcı olarak ayrıca adlandırılır.
Hayvanlara ilişkin yardım paylarını alan veya toplayan görevli, verme eyleminden farklı bir katılımcıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi iki veya daha çok taraf arasında kalan orta, aralık ve iç bölge fikrini verir. Geçici çerçeve, eldeki kalıpları da ayrı kullanım olarak sakladığı sürece bu dalı doğru temsil eder.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, beden organını temel anlam olarak korur; vurma, kesilme, ağrı ve tuzağa yakalanma anlamlarını ayrı türemiş ya da özel kullanımlar olarak gösterir.

Bir tuzağın eli yakalaması da özel bir el durumu olarak adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar el organında birleşir; ayrıca ele vurmayı, eli kesilmiş kişiyi, el ağrısını ve elin tuzağa yakalanmasını bu çekirdeğe bağlı biçimlerde kaydeder.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, önünde ve hemen öncesinde anlamlarını yalnızca belirli iki-el yapısına bağlar ve yalın el sözcüğüne genellemez.

Yağmurdan önce tozun, çatışmadan önce sözlü çekişmenin yükselmesi yakın önceliği örnekler.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yapılan işi, işlenen suçu veya uydurulan yazıyı ellere bağlayarak eylemi doğrudan sahibine yükler. Dalın kişinin kendi yaptığı iş ve doğurduğu sorumluluk olarak kurulması bu vurguyu doğru taşır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, eylem ve sorumluluk anlamını kişinin ellerinin yaptığını söyleyen özel yapılara bağlar; bunu yalın el için genel bir anlam saymaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin yaptığı işi, işlediği kötülüğü veya uydurduğu şeyi ellerine bağlayarak eylemi ona yükler ve sonucundan sorumlu olduğunu vurgular.

facets.statement: Kişinin kendi yaptığı işin doğrudan ona yüklenmesi çekirdek anlamdır.
Yapılan iş bir suç veya kötülük olduğunda ifade kişinin sorumluluğunu belirginleştirir.
Uydurulmuş bir yazının ellere bağlanması, onu yazanların üretip ortaya koyduğunu vurgular.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, ellerin öne çıkarılmasını kişinin kendi yaptığı işi ona yükleyen bir vurgu olarak açıklar; kazanılan sonuç, işlenen suç ve uydurulan yazı bu sorumluluk bağının örnekleridir.
